sourceEvidence.label: WEIR Batch 8 relay decisions and current sibling implementations

assessment.summary: Use a short-lived signed outbound pull relay after the local canary; do not expose Fade through a tunnel or reuse a generic message queue as authority.

nonNegotiables: Fade and WEIR action services remain loopback-only.
The relay carries no action parameters, evidence bodies, credentials, or reusable permits.
Human operator identity and relay transport identity remain distinct.
Expired, revoked, replayed, and ambiguous decisions produce no second effect.
The local Batch 9 canary must pass before relay enablement.
assumptions: No measured relay latency, memory, or queue-volume budget was supplied.
Mission Control remains the authenticated remote operator surface but not the WEIR permit authority.
The unrelated dirty files in the Lugos parent do not alter the inventoried source evidence.

opportunities.title: Preserve human authority across the remote decision boundary
opportunities.summary: Carry one exact human decision to local Fade without exposing Fade or converting a shared service credential into operator authority.
opportunities.diagnosis: Mission Control authenticates a human, but the current server-to-HUD hop forwards a shared credential and no human principal; existing receipt and transport mechanisms do not model expiry, claim, revocation, or workstation acknowledgement.

evidence.claim: D12 requires same-host proof first and forbids solving remote approval by binding Fade or WEIR to a non-loopback address.
Fade binds its authority service to loopback, authenticates distinct named clients, and records the transport principal as actor_id.
HUD command authorization returns a boolean and dispatches without an authenticated human context.
Mission Control checks the operator role but forwards only the parsed command object.
Connecting the existing shared-bearer hop directly to Fade would make human attribution conventional rather than cryptographically bound.

desiredInvariants: Every remote decision is signed and bound to one command_id, proposal_hash, action_id, and work_context_hash.
Fade records the human operator and relay transport principal separately.
The workstation initiates the network connection and local action services remain unreachable from the relay host.
Queue delivery, claim, acknowledgement, expiry, and revocation are durable and idempotent.
The capsule exact-set schema forbids parameters and reusable authority.

options.title: Keep approval local
options.summary: Leave remote WEIR projections read-only and require workstation-local approval.

evidenceCoverage.rationale: It preserves the existing loopback boundary and keeps the remote command disabled.
Human identity is still lost at the HUD hop, but that hop cannot reach action authority.

tradeoffs.assessment: No new remote authority or network path appears.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Verify WEIR decision command definitions remain absent and Fade remains loopback-only.
No benchmark is required beyond existing projection checks.

tradeoffs.assessment: No process, buffer, or queue is added.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Confirm deployment process inventory is unchanged.

tradeoffs.assessment: The local path remains the only action path.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Run the local action canary and verify remote commands stay disabled.

tradeoffs.assessment: No new key, service, or alert is owned.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Check deployed service and credential inventory.

tradeoffs.assessment: No schema or deployment migration occurs.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Keep the relay feature flag absent or false.

residualRisks: A remote operator cannot resolve a time-sensitive proposal.

workPackages: Keep WEIR decisions disabled in remote command registries.
acceptanceCriteria: No remote route can reach Fade decision write scope.

options.title: Tunnel HUD to Fade
options.summary: Use SSH or a tailnet route to make the workstation loopback service reachable from the HUD host.

evidenceCoverage.rationale: The process still binds loopback, but the tunnel creates effective remote reachability.
The human principal remains absent from the forwarded command.
A private carrier narrows exposure but is not application authority.

tradeoffs.assessment: A long-lived path and shared gateway credential can reach Fade without preserving the human principal.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Threat-test host compromise, credential theft, tunnel misbinding, and operator attribution.

tradeoffs.assessment: A live tunnel adds only transport latency and no polling interval.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Measure request latency across the selected tunnel carrier.

tradeoffs.assessment: Only a bounded tunnel process and connection buffers are added.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Measure tunnel process RSS and connection-buffer limits.

tradeoffs.assessment: Availability couples to a persistent connection without explicit offline decision semantics.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Drop the tunnel before and after dispatch and inspect retry behavior.

tradeoffs.assessment: Tunnel lifecycle, ACLs, and gateway credentials require supervision and rotation.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Exercise restart, credential rotation, and tunnel teardown runbooks.

tradeoffs.assessment: It needs less application code than a queue but expands authority before identity is fixed.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Inventory every new route, credential, and bind after a disabled diagnostic.

residualRisks: No durable offline expiry or revocation model.
Host compromise gains a direct Fade path.

workPackages: Diagnostic read-only tunnel only; do not grant decision scope.
acceptanceCriteria: The tunnel cannot submit a WEIR decision.
migrationNotes: Do not treat tailnet membership as application authentication.
implementationReadiness.rollback: Stop the tunnel, revoke its credentials, and verify Fade has no non-loopback listener.

options.title: Signed outbound pull relay
options.summary: Queue signed, short-lived, parameter-free human decisions and let a per-device workstation agent retrieve them over an outbound authenticated connection.

evidenceCoverage.rationale: The workstation initiates transport and Fade remains loopback-only.
Fade can verify and record separate human and transport identities before its existing coordinator.
A signed capsule replaces boolean/shared-bearer identity at the authority transfer.
The authenticated Mission Control operator becomes an explicit signed subject.
Tailscale can protect transport while mTLS and signatures retain application identity.

tradeoffs.assessment: Exact signed bindings, separate identities, expiry, revocation, and outbound-only connectivity narrow the new authority boundary.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Run signature, identity, replay, expiry, revocation, compromised-HUD, and ambiguity tests.

tradeoffs.assessment: Polling, signatures, and acknowledgement add hops; provisional p95 delivery must remain below two seconds.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Measure 1,000 synthetic decisions on normal and degraded links against the two-second p95 target.

tradeoffs.assessment: A bounded agent and queue retain capsule metadata; live entries are capped at 1,024 and capsules at 8 KiB.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Measure peak RSS and database size at the hard queue and capsule bounds.

tradeoffs.assessment: Durable claim and acknowledgement make restart and offline behavior explicit, at the cost of more components.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Crash the issuer, queue, poller, Fade, and each network response boundary and prove no duplicate effect.

tradeoffs.assessment: Operators must own signer keys, per-device credentials, clocks, queue health, agent lifecycle, and incident response.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Exercise key rotation, credential revocation, clock failure, backup/restore, and rollback runbooks.

tradeoffs.assessment: A versioned capsule, queue protocol, step-up flow, poller, and Fade verifier must land disabled across several repositories.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Use frozen cross-repository fixtures and deploy consumer tolerance before producers.

residualRisks: Compromise of the relay signer host.
Coercion or compromise of a legitimate operator endpoint.
Denial of service against queue or poller.
Revocation cannot undo an effect after Fade crosses its dispatch marker.

affectedComponents: lugos-hud or a separate relay service
workPackages: Freeze capsule, queue, acknowledgement, and audit fixtures.
Add Mission Control exact proposal reload and operator step-up.
Add the least-privilege signer and bounded durable queue.
Add the outbound workstation agent and Fade capsule verifier.
Run cross-repository negative, restart, and remote synthetic canaries.
acceptanceCriteria: No network listener exposes Fade or WEIR beyond loopback.
Every accepted capsule carries a distinct human actor and transport principal.
Expired, revoked, replayed, malformed, and ambiguous cases produce no second effect.
The relay never stores or transmits action parameters or reusable permits.
migrationNotes: Keep decision write scope disabled until the local Batch 9 canary and a post-implementation security review pass.
Deploy consumers and verification keys before allowing capsule issuance.
implementationReadiness.rollback: Disable issuance and polling, revoke the device credential, preserve audit state, and continue local approval.

opportunities.recommendation: Select the signed outbound pull relay only after local Batch 9 acceptance; otherwise retain local-only approval.

openQuestions: Which deployed operator identity provider will own WebAuthn/passkey enrollment and recovery?
Will the signer and queue be a separate least-privilege service or share the HUD host process boundary?
What existing audit-retention period should apply to redacted capsule metadata?
Which hostname, CA, and network carrier will provide workstation-to-relay mTLS?
